summary: Restoration and mixed pledges include 160 million additional mangroves by 2030, a 100 million-mangrove project, restoring half of recent mangrove losses, and enhancing negative-emission capacity to −9.3 MtCO2e by 2035; Dubai’s tree-planting target is 100% complete. Conservation commitments include 18.4% protection of terrestrial and inland water and 12.1% of coastal and marine areas (met by 2020), a 30% land-and-sea goal for 2030, and 60% of Dubai’s area preserved as natural areas or reserves by 2040. The UAE endorsed global mangrove and seagrass goals of 15 million hectares and 150,000 km² by 2030, alongside a $4 billion mangrove-investment goal by 2030 and $100 million for nature-climate projects. Of the UAE’s 71,216 km² land area, 87.6% is bare, 3.3% agricultural, and only 33 km² is forest. Low-relevance agriculture entries give an unspecified 39% target and a built-environment water-use endpoint of 2,393 million cubic meters by 2050.
